newsitem.title: USA: USDA reactivates upland cotton payments.
newsitem.headline: USDA reactivates upland cotton payments.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Thursday it will make payments to exporters and manufacturers under the upland cotton user marketing certificate program for the first time since Dec 1, 1994.
USDA said the payment for raw upland cotton processed or shipped for export during the period ending midnight July 17 will be 0.57 cent a lb.

Under the cotton marketing program, also known as "Step 2," if U.S. cotton is priced more than 1.25 cents per pound above an average of the world's five cheapest growths of cotton, it is presumed to be non-competitive and manufacturers and exporters may receive payments.
The department said the payment rate per pound will be recomputed, or eliminated, on July 17 depending on world cotton market conditions between July 11 and July 17.
